p.src: Now Shi Xiu and Lu Junyi, finding no way of escape within the city, were surrounded on every side by troops. The constables caught them with man-catching hooks and tripped them with lassos. Pitifully, those valiant heroes learned at last that the few cannot withstand the many. Both were seized on the spot and taken before Chief Secretary Liang, who ordered the brigands that had stormed the execution ground brought forward. Held below the hall, Shi Xiu glared fiercely and shouted abuse: “You villains who ruin the state and torment the people! I act under my elder brother’s command. Before long he will lead his army here, batter down your city and level it to the ground, then hack you into three pieces! Your lord Shi has merely come ahead to make that clear to you.” Before the hall, Shi Xiu heaped every manner of abuse upon them, calling them villains again and again, until everyone in the hall stood petrified with fright. Chief Secretary Liang listened, pondered for a long while, then ordered heavy cangues brought. He had both men cangued and confined in the condemned prisoners’ ward, instructing Cai Fu to guard them carefully and allow no mishap. Cai Fu wished to gain the friendship of the heroes of Liangshan Marsh, so he locked the two men in the same cell and served them good wine and meat every day. Thus they suffered no hardship and instead recovered their strength. Meanwhile, Chief Secretary Liang summoned the newly appointed Prefect Wang of the prefecture to conduct the proceedings in the hall, while the casualties throughout the city were counted. Seventy or eighty had been killed, while those who had bruised their heads and faces, scraped their flesh, or broken their legs were beyond counting. Their names were reported to the authorities, and Chief Secretary Liang disbursed public funds for medical treatment and burial expenses, thereby settling the matter. The next day, reports came in from within and outside the city: “Several dozen unsigned placards from Liangshan Marsh have been collected. We dared not conceal them and could only present them to you.” When Chief Secretary Liang read them, his wits fled beyond the heavens and his soul scattered through the highest skies. The placards read:

ja: すうじゅうまいかいしゅう
u.src: The next day, reports came in from within and outside the city: “Several dozen unsigned placards from Liangshan Marsh have been collected. We dared not conceal them and could only present them to you.”
When Chief Secretary Liang read them, his wits fled beyond the heavens and his soul scattered through the highest skies.
The placards read:

p.src: Song Jiang, a righteous man of Liangshan Marsh, hereby addresses Daming Prefecture and proclaims to all under Heaven: Corrupt officials now hold sway at the court of the Great Song, and venal functionaries monopolize power, beating innocent people to death and plunging the myriad commoners into misery. Lu Junyi of Beijing is a man of heroic worth. We have now invited him to ascend the mountain and join us in carrying out justice on Heaven’s behalf. How dare you bend the law for treacherous bribers and murder an innocent man! We specially sent Shi Xiu ahead to give warning, but unexpectedly both men were captured. If you preserve both men’s lives and surrender the adulterous woman and her paramour, we shall cause no disturbance. But if you deliberately harm our winged allies and destroy our trusted limbs, we shall strike camp and raise an army, unite in avenging this wrong, and wherever our great host advances, jade and stone alike shall be consumed. We shall root out the treacherous and utterly destroy the obstinate fools. Heaven and Earth shall aid us, and ghosts and spirits alike protect us. We shall enter the city laughing and talking, and grant no leniency whatsoever. Righteous men, chaste women, filial sons, obedient descendants, good people devoted to justice, and upright, prudent officials must not be alarmed; let each remain peacefully at his calling. Let all be duly informed.

Let all be duly informed.

p.src: After reading the unsigned proclamation, Chief Secretary Liang summoned Prefect Wang to consult with him. “How should this matter be decided?” he asked. Prefect Wang was a kindly but timid man. On hearing this, he reported to Chief Secretary Liang: “The imperial court has tried several times to capture the Liangshan Marsh band and still failed. How much less can it be done with the strength of our single prefecture? Should those desperate outlaws lead an army here, and the court’s reinforcements fail to arrive in time, repentance would then come too late! In my humble opinion, we should preserve these two men’s lives for the present, while at the same time drafting a memorial to report the matter to the imperial court. Second, we should submit a letter informing our gracious patron Grand Preceptor Cai. Third, we should order the local forces to leave the city and establish camps, guarding against any unforeseen attack. By doing so, we can keep Beijing safe and spare both soldiers and civilians from harm. If we kill these two out of hand, I truly fear that when the bandit army reaches the city, first, we shall have no troops to deliver us; second, the imperial court will hold us to blame; and third, the people will panic and turmoil will erupt within the city. It would be most inadvisable.” Chief Secretary Liang heard him out and said, “Your words, Prefect, are entirely sound.” He first summoned Cai Fu, the warden in charge of the prison, and said, “These two brigands are no ordinary prisoners. If you restrain them too harshly, I fear they may lose their lives. But if I tell you to be lenient, I fear they may escape. You and your brother must watch them morning and night, tightening or easing their confinement as appropriate. Guard them securely and await judgment; do not neglect your duty for a single moment.” Cai Fu heard this and rejoiced inwardly: “Such instructions are precisely what I wanted.” Having received the order, he returned to the prison and comforted the two men. Of this, no more need be said.

p.src: Chief Secretary Liang then summoned the two military governors, “Great Blade” Wen Da and “Heavenly King” Li Cheng, and both came before the hall to confer. Chief Secretary Liang related in detail the matter of Liangshan Marsh’s unsigned proclamation and what Prefect Wang had advised. When the two military governors had heard him out, Li Cheng said, “How would these mere grass bandits dare leave their lair without authorization? Why need Your Excellency trouble your thoughts over them? Though I, Li, possess little talent, I have long enjoyed my stipend without rendering meritorious service in return. I am willing to labor like a dog or horse, command the troops, leave the city, and establish camp. If the grass bandits do not come, we can consider some other course. But if those fierce brigands, their years and lives nearing their end, dare leave their lair and lead their followers here, then, without boasting, I shall assuredly see that not one scrap of their armor returns!” Chief Secretary Liang was delighted to hear this and immediately brought out gold-flowered embroidered satin to reward the two generals. The two declined with thanks, took leave of Chief Secretary Liang, and returned separately to their camps to rest.

p.src: The next day, Li Cheng ascended the command dais and summoned officers and soldiers of every rank to confer before him. From the side strode forth a man of imposing valor and splendid appearance. It was “Urgent Vanguard” Suo Chao, who came forward to present himself. Li Cheng issued his order: “The grass bandit Song Jiang will reach the city before long and means to attack our Beijing. Muster the troops under your command and establish camp thirty-five li outside the city. I shall follow later with the main force.” Having received his general’s order, Suo Chao mustered the troops under his command the next day and marched thirty-five li to a place called Flying Tiger Ravine, where he set up a stockaded camp against the mountain. The following day, Li Cheng led his senior and subordinate officers twenty-five li outside the city to a place called Locust Tree Slope, where he too established a stockaded camp. Spears and blades were densely arrayed all around, chevaux-de-frise lay concealed on every side, and pits were dug on three approaches. The soldiers rubbed their fists and palms in eagerness, while the generals united their strength and purpose. They waited only for the forces of Liangshan Marsh to arrive so that they might win distinction.

p.src: But now the tale divides and turns to another quarter. It turned out that the anonymous notices had been devised by the Scholar Wu. After Yan Qing and Yang Xiong brought word of what had happened, he sent Dai Zong to investigate and learned that both Squire Lu and Shi Xiu had been arrested. He therefore composed the false proclamation and had copies dropped in deserted places and posted on bridges and along the roads, solely to preserve the lives of Lu Junyi and Shi Xiu. When Dai Zong returned to Liangshan Marsh, he gave the chieftains a full account of all that had happened. Song Jiang was greatly alarmed when he heard the report. He at once had the drum sounded in the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness to summon the company, and all the chieftains, high and low, took their seats in due order. Song Jiang began by saying to the Scholar Wu, “At first, with the best of intentions, you invited Squire Lu to join our brotherhood here on the mountain. Yet now, contrary to all expectation, we have brought suffering upon him and involved our brother Shi Xiu as well. What plan can we use to rescue them?” Wu Yong replied, “Set your mind at ease, brother. Though I am a man of little talent, I have a plan to offer. We can seize this opportunity to capture Beijing’s money and grain for the stronghold’s use. Tomorrow is an auspicious day. I ask you to assign half the chieftains to guard the stronghold, while all the rest accompany us to attack the city.” Song Jiang said, “The strategist’s words are entirely sound.” He then summoned Pei Xuan, the Iron-Faced Registrar, and ordered him to assign the officers and troops for departure the next day. Li Kui, the Black Whirlwind, immediately cried, “These two great axes of mine have gone far too long without any business. When they heard we were going to strike a prefecture and sack a county, even they rejoiced beside the hall. Brother, give me five hundred young fighting men. I shall storm Beijing, hack Grand Secretary Liang into mincemeat, and seize Li Gu and that woman and tear them limb from limb. It is my heart’s desire to save the lives of Squire Lu and Shi Xiu.” Song Jiang said, “Brave as you are, brother, Beijing is unlike any other prefectural city. Moreover, Grand Secretary Liang is the son-in-law of Grand Preceptor Cai, and under his command are Li Cheng and Wen Da, both warriors capable of standing against ten thousand men. We must not underestimate the enemy.” Li Kui shouted, “Brother, why do you raise the enemy’s courage only to dampen our own spirit? Just watch me go and see how I fare! If I should lose, I swear I shall never return to the mountain.” Wu Yong said, “Since you are determined to go, you shall be the vanguard. I shall assign five hundred stout fellows to accompany you. You will form the first assault and descend the mountain tomorrow.” That evening, Song Jiang and Wu Yong conferred together and settled the number of men to be assigned. Pei Xuan wrote out the orders and sent them to every stockade, directing each to carry out its assigned duty without the slightest delay.

p.src: It was then the end of autumn and the beginning of winter, weather in which men on campaign could readily don their armor and warhorses could easily be brought to full condition. The soldiers had long been away from battle, and all were eager to fight; each bitterly resented the injustice and longed to exact revenge. Delighted beyond measure to receive their assignments, they made ready their spears and swords, saddled and harnessed their horses, and rubbed their fists in anticipation, waiting for the moment to descend the mountain.
